You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:
        
CREATE TABLE Student (
    StuID INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    LName VARCHAR(12),
    Fname VARCHAR(12),
    Age INTEGER,
    Sex VARCHAR(1),
    Major INTEGER,
    Advisor INTEGER,
    city_code VARCHAR(3)
);

CREATE TABLE Has_Pet (
    StuID INTEGER,
    PetID INTEGER,
    FOREIGN KEY (StuID) REFERENCES Student(StuID),
    FOREIGN KEY (PetID) REFERENCES Pets(PetID)
);

CREATE TABLE Pets (
    PetID INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    PetType VARCHAR(20),
    pet_age INTEGER,
    weight REAL
);

What kind of “analysis of students” do you want? Here are common SQL analyses you can run on the `Student` table (and pets), and you can tell me which ones you need.

### 1) Basic student counts
```sql
SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_students
FROM Student;
```

### 2) Students by major
```sql
SELECT Major, COUNT(*) AS student_count
FROM Student
GROUP BY Major
ORDER BY student_count DESC;
```

### 3) Students by sex
```sql
SELECT Sex, COUNT(*) AS student_count
FROM Student
GROUP BY Sex
ORDER BY student_count DESC;
```

### 4) Age statistics (min/avg/max) + distribution
```sql
SELECT MIN(Age) AS min_age, AVG(Age) AS avg_age, MAX(Age) AS max_age
FROM Student;
```

```sql
SELECT Age, COUNT(*) AS student_count
FROM Student
GROUP BY Age
ORDER BY Age;
```

### 5) Students by city
```sql
SELECT city_code, COUNT(*) AS student_count
FROM Student
GROUP BY city_code
ORDER BY student_count DESC;
```

### 6) Advisor load (how many students per advisor)
```sql
SELECT Advisor, COUNT(*) AS advisee_count
FROM Student
GROUP BY Advisor
ORDER BY advisee_count DESC;
```

### 7) Pet ownership analysis (who has pets, how many, types)
Students with pet counts (including zero):
```sql
SELECT s.StuID, s.LName, s.Fname, COUNT(hp.PetID) AS pet_count
FROM Student s
LEFT JOIN Has_Pet hp ON hp.StuID = s.StuID
GROUP BY s.StuID, s.LName, s.Fname
ORDER BY pet_count DESC, s.StuID;
```

Pet types owned:
```sql
SELECT p.PetType, COUNT(*) AS owned_count
FROM Has_Pet hp
JOIN Pets p ON p.PetID = hp.PetID
GROUP BY p.PetType
ORDER BY owned_count DESC;
```

Tell me what you mean by “analysis” (e.g., age/sex breakdown, major distribution, advisor load, pets), and whether you want results overall or filtered (by major, city_code, age range, etc.).
I need the analysis for students who have pets.

Here are useful analyses limited to **students who have pets** (i.e., appear in `Has_Pet`).

### 1) List students who have pets + how many
```sql
SELECT s.StuID, s.LName, s.Fname, COUNT(*) AS pet_count
FROM Student s
JOIN Has_Pet hp ON hp.StuID = s.StuID
GROUP BY s.StuID, s.LName, s.Fname
ORDER BY pet_count DESC, s.StuID;
```

### 2) Student demographics (pet owners only): sex breakdown
```sql
SELECT s.Sex, COUNT(DISTINCT s.StuID) AS student_count
FROM Student s
JOIN Has_Pet hp ON hp.StuID = s.StuID
GROUP BY s.Sex
ORDER BY student_count DESC;
```

### 3) Pet-owner age stats
```sql
SELECT MIN(s.Age) AS min_age,
       AVG(s.Age) AS avg_age,
       MAX(s.Age) AS max_age
FROM Student s
JOIN Has_Pet hp ON hp.StuID = s.StuID;
```

### 4) Pet owners by major
```sql
SELECT s.Major, COUNT(DISTINCT s.StuID) AS student_count
FROM Student s
JOIN Has_Pet hp ON hp.StuID = s.StuID
GROUP BY s.Major
ORDER BY student_count DESC;
```

### 5) Pet owners by city
```sql
SELECT s.city_code, COUNT(DISTINCT s.StuID) AS student_count
FROM Student s
JOIN Has_Pet hp ON hp.StuID = s.StuID
GROUP BY s.city_code
ORDER BY student_count DESC;
```

### 6) What kinds of pets do students have (counts by type)
```sql
SELECT p.PetType, COUNT(*) AS pet_count
FROM Has_Pet hp
JOIN Pets p ON p.PetID = hp.PetID
GROUP BY p.PetType
ORDER BY pet_count DESC;
```

### 7) Pet details owned by each student (type/age/weight)
```sql
SELECT s.StuID, s.LName, s.Fname,
       p.PetID, p.PetType, p.pet_age, p.weight
FROM Student s
JOIN Has_Pet hp ON hp.StuID = s.StuID
JOIN Pets p ON p.PetID = hp.PetID
ORDER BY s.StuID, p.PetID;
```

If you tell me what “analysis” format you need (single summary query vs multiple tables, and whether you want majors/cities/sex/age), I can combine it into one report.
include first names of students too

All of the student-focused queries can include first names by selecting `s.Fname` (and grouping by it when aggregating). Here are the main ones with first names included:

### Students who have pets + how many (includes first name)
```sql
SELECT s.StuID, s.Fname, s.LName, COUNT(*) AS pet_count
FROM Student s
JOIN Has_Pet hp ON hp.StuID = s.StuID
GROUP BY s.StuID, s.Fname, s.LName
ORDER BY pet_count DESC, s.StuID;
```

### Pet details per student (includes first name)
```sql
SELECT s.StuID, s.Fname, s.LName,
       p.PetID, p.PetType, p.pet_age, p.weight
FROM Student s
JOIN Has_Pet hp ON hp.StuID = s.StuID
JOIN Pets p ON p.PetID = hp.PetID
ORDER BY s.StuID, p.PetID;
```

### Pet owners by major (includes first name in output list)
If you want a per-student breakdown by major:
```sql
SELECT s.Major, s.StuID, s.Fname, s.LName, COUNT(hp.PetID) AS pet_count
FROM Student s
JOIN Has_Pet hp ON hp.StuID = s.StuID
GROUP BY s.Major, s.StuID, s.Fname, s.LName
ORDER BY s.Major, pet_count DESC;
```

Tell me which output you want: **(A)** one row per student with `pet_count`, or **(B)** one row per student per pet with pet details.
Include the ages of the students too.

### A) One row per student (pet owners) with first name + age + pet count
```sql
SELECT s.StuID, s.Fname, s.LName, s.Age, COUNT(*) AS pet_count
FROM Student s
JOIN Has_Pet hp ON hp.StuID = s.StuID
GROUP BY s.StuID, s.Fname, s.LName, s.Age
ORDER BY pet_count DESC, s.StuID;
```

### B) One row per pet (pet owners) with student first name + age + pet details
```sql
SELECT s.StuID, s.Fname, s.LName, s.Age,
       p.PetID, p.PetType, p.pet_age, p.weight
FROM Student s
JOIN Has_Pet hp ON hp.StuID = s.StuID
JOIN Pets p ON p.PetID = hp.PetID
ORDER BY s.StuID, p.PetID;
```
